secoes.corpo:
A geriatric assessment differs from conventional clinical assessment due to its multidimensional nature: the elderly often present multiple interrelated chronic conditions that cannot be assessed in isolation. The so-called "geriatric syndromes" — falls, functional decline, depression, cognitive impairment, and frailty — require specific and validated instruments for this population.

A The Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) , developed by Yesavage et al. in 1983, is the most widely used screening instrument for depression in the elderly. Unlike other depression scales, the GDS avoids somatic symptoms (fatigue, appetite changes, insomnia) that can be confused with the aging process itself or with clinical comorbidities. Its reduced 15-item version (GDS-15) is quick (3-5 minutes) and widely validated in Brazilian Portuguese.

A functional assessment with the Barthel Index and the fall risk assessment with Morse (hospital) or Downton (geriatric/community) complete the triad of geriatric assessment. The integration of these instruments allows identifying the elderly at risk of adverse outcomes and planning targeted preventive interventions.

Introduction to Geriatric Scales
A geriatric assessment differs from conventional clinical assessment due to its multidimensional nature: the elderly often present multiple interrelated chronic conditions that cannot be assessed in isolation. Unlike other depression scales, the GDS avoids somatic symptoms (fatigue, appetite changes, insomnia) that can be confused with the aging process itself or with clinical comorbidities. Its reduced 15-item version (GDS-15) is quick (3-5 minutes) and widely validated in Brazilian Portuguese.

A functional assessment with the Barthel Index and the fall risk assessment with Morse (hospital) or Downton (geriatric/community) complete the triad of geriatric assessment. The integration of these instruments allows identifying the elderly at risk of adverse outcomes and planning targeted preventive interventions.

When to Use Each Scale

Comparison of Geriatric Scales

Scales and Calculators

GDS
Geriatric Depression Scale

Screening for depression in the elderly. 15 YES/NO questions. Score 0-15. > 5 = probable depression. Avoids somatic symptoms.

Barthel
Functional Independence

Assessment of Activities of Daily Living. 10 items, score 0-100. Essential for geriatric care planning.

Morse
Fall Risk

Hospital gold standard for fall risk. 6 items. Essential on admission of elderly patients to inpatient units.

Falls in the Elderly

Specific assessment for the elderly. 5 items, score 0-11. Ideal for LTCF and home care.
